dohas.gahraBhav: 'Adham udhaar' — the greatest mark of the Satguru is that he delivers even the most fallen and lowly. None is excluded from his grace.

dohas.title: Alal pankh anuraag hai...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, alal pankh anuraag hai, sunn mandal rahai theer.
Daas Garib udhaariya, Satguru mile Kabir || 100 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Love for the unseen (alakh) wings; devotion to the formless
Remains steady in the sphere of the void
The servant Garib was delivered

dohas.saralarth: There is love for the unseen, and he remains steady in the sphere of the void. The servant Garib was delivered — for the Satguru Kabir was found.
dohas.gahraBhav: This is the closing couplet of the Ang. 'Satguru mile Kabir' — this is the proclamation of Garibdas Ji's supreme realization. All the practice, all the journey, all the struggle — all of it was for this one union.

dohas.title: Satguru daata hain kali maahin...
dohas.fullText:
Satguru daata hain kali maahin, praan udhaaran utre Saain.
Satguru daata deen dayaaloon, jam ki kar ke torain jaaloon || 1 ||

shabdarth.meaning: In the Kali age (the present dark age)
The deliverer of life; one who redeems the soul
Lord; master

shabdarth.word: jam ki kar ke torain jaaloon
shabdarth.meaning: Breaks apart the snare of Yama (death) with his own hand

dohas.saralarth: In the Kali age the Satguru alone is the true bestower. He is the Lord (Saain) who has descended to redeem souls. He is gracious to the lowly and tears apart the snare of Yama (death).
dohas.gahraBhav: In the Kali age other disciplines are arduous, but the grace of the Satguru is accessible. 'Tearing the snare of Yama' means liberation from the cycle of death and rebirth.

dohas.title: Satguru daata daya karaanhin...
dohas.fullText:
Satguru daata daya karaanhin, agam deep sain so chal aahin.
Satguru bina panth nahin paavai, Satguru milain to alakh lakhaavain || 2 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Comes traveling from the unreachable isle (the supreme abode)
The path is not found
Reveals the unseen Supreme Being (Alakh)

dohas.saralarth: The Satguru shows grace and comes traveling from the unreachable supreme abode. Without him the path is not found — when he is met, he reveals the unseen Supreme Being.
dohas.gahraBhav: The Satguru comes of his own will from the supreme realm to redeem devotees. This is compassionate grace.

dohas.title: Satguru Sahib ek shareera...
dohas.fullText:
Satguru Sahib ek shareera, Satguru bina na laagai teera.
Satguru baan vihangam maarain, Satguru bhav saagar sain taarain || 3 ||

shabdarth.meaning: One single body — the Sahib and the Satguru are non-different
One does not reach the shore
Strikes the soaring arrow — releases the divine arrow

dohas.saralarth: The Sahib and the Satguru are one single body. Without the Satguru one cannot reach the shore. He strikes the soaring divine arrow and ferries one across the ocean of existence.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'One single body' — the Sahib and the Satguru are inseparable. Serving the Guru and serving the Supreme Being are one and the same.

dohas.title: Satguru bina na paavai painda...
dohas.fullText:
Satguru bina na paavai painda, hanth haath gadh leejai kainda.
Satguru darad boond devesa, jo man kar hai door andesha || 4 ||

shabdarth.meaning: The path; the way
Takes one by the hand and lifts one onto his shoulder
Gives a drop of pain — bestows the ache of spiritual longing
Removes the distant dread / anxiety

dohas.saralarth: Without the Satguru the path is not found. He takes one by the hand and lifts one onto his shoulder. He gives that drop of pain (longing) which removes every distant dread.
dohas.gahraBhav: The Satguru does not leave the disciple alone. 'A drop of pain' is the ache of spiritual separation that awakens the seeker.

dohas.title: Satguru darad boond darbaari...
dohas.fullText:
Satguru darad boond darbaari, utre Sahib sunn adhaari.
Satguru Sahib ang na dooja, ye sagun vai nirgun pooja || 5 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Of the supreme court
Descended upon the support of the void (sunn)
No second form — one and the same
This one is the manifest (sagun); that one the unmanifest (nirgun) — worship of both is one

dohas.saralarth: The Satguru is the drop of pain of the supreme court, the Sahib who descended upon the support of the void. The Sahib and the Satguru are not two forms — this is worship of the manifest, that of the unmanifest.
dohas.gahraBhav: The oneness of the manifest (sagun) and the unmanifest (nirgun) — serving the Satguru is itself the worship of the Supreme Being.

dohas.title: Sakhi — nirgun sagun ek hai...
dohas.fullText:
Sakhi — Garib, nirgun sagun ek hai, dooja bharam vikaar.
Nirgun Sahib aap hain sagun sant vichaar || 1 ||

shabdarth.meaning: The formless and the formed are one and the same
To regard the two as separate is delusion
The formless is the Sahib himself
The saint is the formed reflection — the manifest aspect

dohas.saralarth: The formless (nirgun) and the formed (sagun) are one and the same — to regard them as separate is delusion and distortion. The Sahib himself is the formless, and the saint is his formed reflection (the manifest aspect).
dohas.gahraBhav: This sakhi gives the highest message of non-duality. The distinction between formless and formed is only a matter of perception, not of essence.

dohas.title: Satguru Sahib akal aleelam...
dohas.fullText:
Satguru Sahib akal aleelam, ja ke panth na chadhe papeelam.
Satguru mahima kya gaaun, harsh-harsh charanaun chit laaun || 1 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Beyond parts and beyond play — utterly free of flaw
An ant — even the tiniest creature cannot climb
With joy, again and again in bliss
I fix my mind, I meditate

dohas.saralarth: The Satguru Sahib is beyond parts and beyond flaw — upon his path not even an ant can climb. How can I sing the Satguru's glory — joyfully I fix my mind upon his feet.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Upon whose path not even an ant can climb' — his way is so subtle that the petty intellect cannot reach it.

dohas.title: Satguru Sahib aahi anaaham...
dohas.fullText:
Satguru Sahib aahi anaaham, jaako khojat hain sur saadham.
Jo Satguru ke sharanai aavai, aanand-ghan pad maahin samaavain || 2 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Is, and is the unstruck (anahad) — present and soundless-sound
Gods and holy seekers
The supreme state brimming with bliss

dohas.saralarth: The Satguru Sahib is the unstruck — whom gods and holy ones seek. Whoever comes to his shelter merges into the bliss-laden supreme state.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Bliss-laden state' — a state full of bliss like a dense cloud. Taking shelter alone is enough.

dohas.title: Satguru daya karain hil phere...
dohas.fullText:
Satguru daya karain hil phere, koti timir mit jaahin andhere.
Satguru bank naal ho aaye, Shiv Brahmaadik paar na paaye || 3 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Stirs and turns about — changes one's direction
Ten million darknesses
Came through the curved channel (bank naal)
Even Shiva and Brahma could not reach the limit

dohas.saralarth: When the Satguru shows grace and stirs one, ten million darknesses are dispelled. He came through the curved channel — where even Shiva and Brahma could not reach the far shore.
dohas.gahraBhav: Where Shiva and Brahma could not arrive, the Satguru came by the path of the 'bank naal' — this is his distinction.

dohas.title: Satguru bank naal bairaatha...
dohas.fullText:
Satguru bank naal bairaatha, Satguru utre aughat ghaata.
Satguru saar vastu batlaavain, purush vivekee koon darshaavain || 4 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Seated within the curved channel — the abode of Bairath
Descended the difficult, treacherous ford
Reveals the essential substance (the truth)
Reveals it to the discerning person

dohas.saralarth: The Satguru is seated in the Bairath of the curved channel, having descended the treacherous ford. He reveals the essential substance and shows it to the discerning soul.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'The essential substance' — that which is the essence within all, the soul. 'The discerning person' — one who can see beyond mind and illusion.

dohas.title: Satguru Sahib chumbak rupa...
dohas.fullText:
Satguru Sahib chumbak rupa, lagi thakthaki chhaanhi na dhoopa.
Sahib sain Satguru ban aaye, bhaav bhakti le birad badhaaye || 5 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Magnet-like — one who draws all in
An unwavering, fixed gaze
Neither shade nor sun — he is beyond both
Took up loving devotion and upheld his vow

dohas.saralarth: The Satguru Sahib is magnet-like. The gaze stays fixed upon him — he is neither shade nor sun. From the Sahib he became the Satguru and upheld the vow of loving devotion.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Magnet-like' — the Satguru draws one in. In his presence one forgets everything.

dohas.title: Satguru sa daata nahin koi...
dohas.fullText:
Satguru sa daata nahin koi, taaran taran adhar mag joi.
Satguru param dhaam pravaani, Satguru lyaaye agam nishaani || 6 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Ferries others and is himself ferried across
Knower of the path through the heavens (the airy way)
Authenticated by the supreme abode
The sign of the unreachable — the supreme mark

dohas.saralarth: There is no bestower like the Satguru — he has himself crossed over and ferries others across. He is authenticated by the supreme abode and has brought the sign of the unreachable.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Crossed and crosses others' — only one who has himself reached the far shore can carry others across.

dohas.title: Satguru bina surati nahin paahai...
dohas.fullText:
Satguru bina surati nahin paahai, khel mandya hain sir ke saahai.
Satguru bhakti-mukti ke daani, Satguru bina na chhootai khaani || 7 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Inner consciousness (surati) is not attained
At the cost of one's head — by surrendering the head
The bestower of devotion and liberation
The womb of births — the cycle of birth and death

dohas.saralarth: Without the Satguru inner consciousness is not attained. This game is played at the cost of one's head. The Satguru is the bestower of devotion and liberation — without him there is no escape from the cycle of birth and death.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'At the cost of the head' — the sacrifice of the ego is the key to inner consciousness.

dohas.title: Satguru saala karm bataavain...
dohas.fullText:
Satguru saala karm bataavain, Satguru agam deep le jaavain.
Satguru adlee bandh baithaavain, ujad nagri bahur basaavain || 8 ||

shabdarth.meaning: The work of the school — the act of teaching
Takes one to the unreachable realm
Seats one justly and orderly
Resettles the ruined city

dohas.saralarth: The Satguru does the work of teaching and takes one to the unreachable realm. He seats one justly and resettles the ruined city (the soul).
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Resettles the ruined city' — the soul laid waste by illusion is repopulated and revived by the Satguru.

dohas.title: Satguru mukti maalvai daani...
dohas.fullText:
Satguru mukti maalvai daani, Satguru bina na paltai baani.
Satguru bhedee bhed lakhaai, kaaga sain hansa ho jaai || 9 ||

shabdarth.meaning: The bestower who gives the garland of liberation
His word does not turn back — his promise is firm
The knower of the mystery revealed the mystery
Turned a crow into a swan

dohas.saralarth: The Satguru is the bestower of the garland of liberation, and his word is unshakeable. The knower of the mystery revealed the mystery and turned the crow-like soul into a swan.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'From crow to swan' — the crow symbolizes ignorance, the swan symbolizes wisdom. The Guru's grace works this transformation.

dohas.title: Satguru sakal mool mahmanta...
dohas.fullText:
Satguru sakal mool mahmanta, Satguru bina na paavai panthaa.
Satguru adhar-dhaar adhikaari, Satguru kholain swarg dwaari || 10 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Knower of the root-mantra of all that is
Master of the celestial stream
The gate of heaven

dohas.saralarth: The Satguru is the knower of the root-mantra of all — without him the path is not found. He is master of the celestial stream and opens the gate of heaven.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Knower of the root-mantra of all' — only one who knows the root secret of creation is the true Satguru.

dohas.title: Satguru sankh swarg sain nyaare...
dohas.fullText:
Satguru sankh swarg sain nyaare, lipain chhipe nahin harain na haare.
Satguru sakal sunn mein khelain, bhavsaagar se nauka pelain || 11 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Conch-like, set apart even from heaven
Neither smeared by illusion nor hidden
Plays within the void
Rows the boat — ferries across

dohas.saralarth: The Satguru is set apart even from heaven — neither smeared by illusion, nor hidden, nor ever defeated. He plays within the void and rows the boat across the ocean of existence.
dohas.gahraBhav: Living in the world, the Satguru is yet beyond it — like the lotus that stays in water yet rises above it.

dohas.title: Satguru bina sakal sab andha...
dohas.fullText:
Satguru bina sakal sab andha, Satguru kaahain jam ke phanda.
Satguru jaamni-maran mitaavain, Satguru sukh saagar le jaavain || 12 ||

shabdarth.meaning: All are blind — all are ignorant
Cuts the noose of Yama (death)
Erases birth and death
Carries one into the ocean of bliss

dohas.saralarth: Without the Satguru all are blind. He cuts the noose of Yama, erases birth and death, and carries one into the ocean of bliss.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'All are blind' — without self-knowledge everyone is blind. This stern truth proves the necessity of a Guru.

dohas.title: Satguru sukh saagar ki seeree...
dohas.fullText:
Satguru sukh saagar ki seeree, Satguru bina na bandhe dheeree.
Satguru sukh saagar ke hansa, Satguru melat hain kul bansa || 13 ||

shabdarth.meaning: The ladder to the ocean of bliss
Patience does not hold
The swan of the ocean of bliss
The entire lineage — the whole tradition

dohas.saralarth: The Satguru is the ladder to the ocean of bliss — without him patience does not hold. He is the swan of the ocean of bliss and unites the entire lineage.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Seeree' means ladder. The Satguru is the ladder that reaches from the earth to the supreme abode.

dohas.title: Satguru neer kheer koon chhaanai...
dohas.fullText:
Satguru neer kheer koon chhaanai, Satguru baithe haras hivaanai.
Akal aleel agam anuraagi, Satguru milain taas badbhaagi || 14 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Separates milk from water — sifts essence from non-essence
Joyfully in the court — in the court of bliss
Lover of the partless, playless, unreachable One
Greatly fortunate

dohas.saralarth: The Satguru separates milk from water and sits joyfully in his court. He is the lover of the partless, playless and unreachable One — whoever finds him is greatly fortunate.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Greatly fortunate' — meeting the Satguru is the fruit of great fortune. It is no accident, but the result of past deeds and divine grace.

dohas.title: Sakhi — Satguru milain sandeh sab...
dohas.fullText:
Sakhi — Garib, Satguru milain sandeh sab, chhooten bharam vikaar.
Samrath ka sharanaa liya, ham chaakar darbaar || 2 ||

shabdarth.meaning: All doubts fall away
Delusion and distortion
The shelter of the all-capable One
A servant of the court

dohas.saralarth: On meeting the Satguru all doubts fall away, and delusion and distortion are dispelled. I have taken the shelter of the all-capable One — now I am a servant of his court.
dohas.gahraBhav: The spirit of surrender — 'I am a servant of the court'. Casting off ego and taking on the attitude of servitude is the very root of devotion.

dohas.title: Satguru agam bhoomi sain aaye...
dohas.fullText:
Satguru agam bhoomi sain aaye, karm kaand jeev bandh chhutaaye.
Sapt bhoomika bhay nahin koi, dasaun disha ekai mag joi || 1 ||

shabdarth.meaning: The unreachable realm — the supreme abode
The ritual bondage of the soul
The seven realms — the seven levels
Saw one single path

dohas.saralarth: The Satguru came from the unreachable realm and freed the soul from the bondage of rituals. Through the seven realms there is no fear — in all ten directions he saw a single path.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'A single path in all ten directions' — when the Guru's grace is present, the one Supreme Being is seen on every side.

dohas.title: Sapt sunn mein vicharan laaga...
dohas.fullText:
Sapt sunn mein vicharan laaga, divya dekhya anuraaga.
Akal aleel bhoomika bhaari, sab soorat sain moorat nyaari || 2 ||

shabdarth.meaning: The seven voids — the seven states of the soul
Saw the divine with love
A form distinct from all forms

dohas.saralarth: He began to wander through the seven voids and lovingly beheld the divine. A vast unreachable realm — a form distinct from all forms (the form of the Supreme).
dohas.gahraBhav: 'The seven voids' — the seven void-states of spiritual practice. Passing through them, one beholds the divine form.

dohas.title: Ja moorat ka kahoon viveka...
dohas.fullText:
Ja moorat ka kahoon viveka, Satguru bina kaun koon dekha.
Sindh shabd mein kaise mil hain, bin pag panthi kaise chal hain || 3 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Of which form shall I speak the discernment
In the ocean of the Word (shabd)
A wayfarer without feet — one who travels without a body

dohas.saralarth: Of which form shall I speak — without the Satguru, who has seen it? How can one meet it within the ocean of the Word? How can a wayfarer without feet walk?
dohas.gahraBhav: Without the Guru, beholding that supreme form is impossible. 'A wayfarer without feet' — the capacity to travel beyond the body is given by the Guru.

dohas.title: Maarg bina chalan hai tera...
dohas.fullText:
Maagur bina chalan hai tera, Satguru metain timar andhera.
Apne praan daan jo karaahin, tan man dhan sab apun dhar hin || 4 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Walking without a path
Dense darkness
Make one's own — offer in surrender

dohas.saralarth: You are walking without a path — the Satguru dispels the dense darkness. Offer your very life-breath, and surrender body, mind and wealth — all of it.
dohas.gahraBhav: The message of surrender — body, mind and wealth all offered to the Guru. This is the foundation of spiritual practice.

dohas.title: Satguru sankh kala darsaavai...
dohas.fullText:
Satguru sankh kala darsaavai, Satguru ashu vimaan bithaavain.
Satguru bhavsaagar ke kolee, Satguru paar nibaahein dolee || 5 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Reveals conch-like arts — divine powers
A divine vehicle — the chariot of the soul
A boatman, a ferryman
A palanquin — a boat

dohas.saralarth: The Satguru reveals divine arts and seats one upon a celestial vehicle. He is the boatman of the ocean of existence and carries one safely across.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Ashu vimaan' — a divine craft. The grace of the Satguru is that vehicle which carries the seeker to the supreme abode.

dohas.title: Satguru maadar pidar hamaare...
dohas.fullText:
Satguru maadar pidar hamaare, bhausaagar ke taaran haare.
Satguru sundar rup apaara, Satguru teen lok se nyaara || 6 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Mother and father (Persian)
The one who ferries across
A form of boundless beauty
Set apart from all three worlds

dohas.saralarth: The Satguru is our mother and father, the one who ferries us across the ocean of existence. His form is of boundless beauty and he is set apart from all three worlds.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Mother and father' — the Guru is both mother and father, the deepest and most sacred of relationships.

dohas.title: Satguru param padaarth poora...
dohas.fullText:
Satguru param padaarth poora, Satguru bina na baajain toora.
Satguru avaadaan kar devain, Satguru Ram rasaayan bhevain || 7 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Full of the supreme substance — the supreme treasure
The trumpet of victory does not sound
Grants a boon
Reveals the secret of the Ram-elixir

dohas.saralarth: The Satguru is full of the supreme substance — without him the trumpet of victory does not sound. He grants the boon and reveals the secret of the elixir of Ram (the Name).
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Ram rasaayan' — the Name of Ram is that nectar which liberates from death and rebirth.

dohas.title: Satguru pashu maanas kar daarain...
dohas.fullText: Satguru pashu maanas kar daarain, siddh dev kar Brahm vichaarain || 8 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Turns the beast-like into a human being
Makes one an adept and a god
Brings about contemplation of Brahman — bestows divine knowledge

dohas.saralarth: The Satguru turns the beast-like into a human being, makes one an adept and a god, and bestows the contemplation of Brahman.
dohas.gahraBhav: The grace of the Satguru works a gradual transformation — beast to human, to adept, to god, to knower of Brahman.

dohas.title: Sakhi — Brahm binaani hot hain...
dohas.fullText:
Sakhi — Garib, Brahm binaani hot hain Satguru sharanaaleen.
Soobhar soi jaaniye, sab seti aadheen || 3 ||

shabdarth.meaning: A knower of Brahman
Surrendered, taken refuge
Complete, full
Humble toward all

dohas.saralarth: By coming to the shelter of the Satguru one becomes a knower of Brahman. The complete one is he who is humble and yielding toward all.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Humble toward all' — the fruit of wisdom is humility. One who becomes proud through knowledge is not truly wise.

dohas.title: Gyaan saagar ati ujaagar...
dohas.fullText:
Gyaan saagar ati ujaagar, nirvikaar Niranjanoon.
Brahmgyaani mahaadhyaani, sat sukrit dukh bhanjanoon || 1 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Intensely luminous, radiant
Flawless and untainted (Niranjan)
Destroyer of sorrow

dohas.saralarth: That Supreme Being is an ocean of knowledge and intensely luminous — flawless and untainted. The knower of Brahman and the great meditator — the doer of good deeds and the destroyer of sorrow.
dohas.gahraBhav: The Brahm-Vedi opens with the qualities of the Supreme Being. 'Ocean of knowledge' — he is knowledge itself, not merely a vessel of knowledge.

dohas.title: Mool chakra Ganesh baasa...
dohas.fullText:
Mool chakra Ganesh baasa, rakt varn jahaan jaaniye.
Kiliyoon jaap kuleen taj sab, shabd hamaara maaniye || 2 ||

shabdarth.meaning: The Muladhara (root) chakra
The colour red
Recitation of the seed-mantra 'Kleem'
Renounce pride of lineage

dohas.saralarth: In the Muladhara chakra dwells Ganesh, where the colour is red. Recite the seed-mantra 'Kleem' — renounce pride of lineage and accept our word.
dohas.gahraBhav: The Muladhara is the lowest chakra of the body, from which the kundalini power awakens. Ganesh is seated here.

dohas.title: Swaad chakra Brahmaadi baasa...
dohas.fullText:
Swaad chakra Brahmaadi baasa, jahaan Saavitri Brahma rahain.
Om jaap japant hansa, gyaan jog Satguru kahain || 3 ||

shabdarth.meaning: The Svadhishthana chakra
The dwelling of Brahma and others
Recitation of the seed-mantra Om

dohas.saralarth: In the Svadhishthana chakra dwell Brahma and Savitri. The Satguru says — let the swan-soul recite the Om mantra — this is the yoga of knowledge.
dohas.gahraBhav: The Svadhishthana is the centre of creativity and the water element. Brahma resides here as the creative power.

dohas.title: Naabhi kamal mein Vishnu Vishambhar...
dohas.fullText:
Naabhi kamal mein Vishnu Vishambhar, jahaan Lakshmi sang baas hai.
Hariyoon jaap japant hansa, jaati birla daas hai || 4 ||

shabdarth.meaning: The Manipura chakra — the navel lotus
Sustainer of all, the upholder of the world
Recitation of the seed-mantra 'Hreem'

dohas.saralarth: In the navel lotus (Manipura) dwell Vishnu and Lakshmi. Let the swan-soul recite 'Hreem' — rare is the devotee who becomes such a servant.
dohas.gahraBhav: The Manipura is the centre of the fire element and the power of sustenance. Vishnu resides here as the sustainer.

dohas.title: Hriday kamal Mahaadev devoon...
dohas.fullText:
Hriday kamal Mahaadev devoon, Sati Paarvati sang hai.
Sohang jaap japant hansa, gyaan jog bhal rang hai || 5 ||

shabdarth.meaning: The Anahata chakra — the heart lotus
Recitation of the seed-mantra Sohang
Is a fine hue — a beautiful form

dohas.saralarth: In the heart lotus (Anahata) dwell Mahadev and Parvati. Let the swan-soul recite 'Sohang' — this is the beautiful form of the yoga of knowledge.
dohas.gahraBhav: The Anahata is the centre of love and the air element. 'Sohang' resounds here of its own accord.

dohas.title: Kanth kamal mein basai avidya...
dohas.fullText:
Kanth kamal mein basai avidya, gyaan dhyaan buddhi naashahi.
Leel chakra madhya kaal karmam, aavat dam koon phaansahi || 6 ||

shabdarth.meaning: The Vishuddha chakra — the throat lotus
Ignorance
The blue chakra — the Vishuddha
Ensnares every incoming breath

dohas.saralarth: In the throat lotus (Vishuddha) dwells ignorance, which destroys knowledge and meditation. Within the blue chakra is the action of Time, which ensnares every breath.
dohas.gahraBhav: Ignorance dwelling at the Vishuddha — this is the obstacle encountered upon reaching that level.

dohas.title: Trikuti kamal param hans poorn...
dohas.fullText:
Trikuti kamal param hans poorn, Satguru samrath aap hai.
Man pauna sam sindh melo, surati nirati ka jaap hai || 7 ||

shabdarth.meaning: The Ajna chakra — the lotus between the brows
The perfect supreme swan — the Supreme Being
Make mind and breath equal and merge them in the ocean
The practice of surati-nirati (soul-attention)

dohas.saralarth: In the Trikuti (Ajna chakra) the perfect supreme swan, the Satguru himself, abides. Make mind and breath equal and merge them in the ocean — this is the practice of surati-nirati.
dohas.gahraBhav: The Trikuti is the point between the brows, the third eye. The Satguru dwells here. 'Mind and breath made equal' — the state of equipoise.

dohas.title: Sahans kamal dal bhi aap Sahib...
dohas.fullText:
Sahans kamal dal bhi aap Sahib, jyoon phoolan madhya gandh hai.
Poor rahya Jagdeesh jogi, sat samrath nirbandh hai || 8 ||

shabdarth.meaning: The Sahasrara — the thousand-petalled lotus
Like the fragrance within flowers
Is free of all bondage

dohas.saralarth: Even in the Sahasrara lotus the Sahib himself abides — like fragrance within flowers. That Jagdish-yogi pervades all, complete and all-capable, free of bondage.
dohas.gahraBhav: The Sahasrara is the highest chakra, where the Supreme Being pervades like fragrance in a flower.

dohas.title: Meeni khoj hanoj hardam...
dohas.fullText:
Meeni khoj hanoj hardam, ulat panth ki baat hai.
Ila Pingula Sushman khojo, chal hansa aughat ghaat hai || 9 ||

shabdarth.meaning: The subtle search, the inward quest
The reverse path — inward-turned practice
The three channels — Ida, Pingala and Sushumna

dohas.saralarth: Search subtly at every moment — this is the way of the reverse path. Seek out Ida, Pingala and Sushumna — move on, swan-soul, the ford is treacherous.
dohas.gahraBhav: Meditation upon the three channels and traveling them by the reverse path — this is the secret of kundalini practice.

dohas.title: Aisa jog vijog varno...
dohas.fullText:
Aisa jog vijog varno, jo Shankar ne chit dharya.
Kumbhak rechak dwaadas palte, kaal karm tis tain darya || 10 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Union and separation — joining and parting
The breath-retention and exhalation practices
Turned twelve times over
Time and karma grow afraid

dohas.saralarth: Such is the account of union and separation that Shankar held in his mind. Let kumbhak and rechak turn twelve times — Time and karma grow afraid of it.
dohas.gahraBhav: A special method of breath-control — through kumbhak and rechak the fear of Time is destroyed.

dohas.title: Sunn singhaasan amar aasan...
dohas.fullText:
Sunn singhaasan amar aasan, alakh purush nirvaan hai.
Ati lyauleen bedeen maalik, kaadar koon kurbaan hai || 11 ||

shabdarth.meaning: The throne of the void — the supreme seat
Nirvana — supreme liberation
Absorbed and beyond want
The Almighty — Qadir (Arabic)

dohas.saralarth: The throne of the void is the immortal seat — there the unseen Being abides in nirvana. He is the deeply absorbed and wantless Master — I am a sacrifice to that Almighty.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'The throne of the void' — emptiness itself is the seat of the Supreme Being. 'Kaadar' is an Arabic word — the Almighty.

dohas.title: Hai nirsingh abandh anbigat...
dohas.fullText:
Hai nirsingh abandh anbigat, koti baikunth khirup hai.
Aparampaar deedaar darshan, aisa ajab anoop hai || 12 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Lion-like — fearless, the man-lion
Free of bondage and imperceptible
The form of ten million Vaikunthas
Boundless vision

dohas.saralarth: He is lion-like, free of bondage and imperceptible — the form of ten million Vaikunthas. His vision is boundless — so wondrous and incomparable is he.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'The form of ten million Vaikunthas' — the Supreme Being is the source of countless Vaikunthas. He is not confined to any single realm.

dohas.title: Ghurain nisaan akhand dhun sun...
dohas.fullText:
Ghurain nisaan akhand dhun sun, Sohang bedi gaaiye.
Baajain naad agaadh ag hai, jahaan le man thahraaiye || 13 ||

shabdarth.meaning: The banner resounds
The unbroken unstruck sound (anahad naad)
The altar of Sohang — the seat
Unfathomable and unreachable

dohas.saralarth: The unbroken sound resounds — sing it upon the altar of Sohang. The unfathomable unstruck sound plays — there bring the mind to rest.
dohas.gahraBhav: Meditation upon the unstruck sound — stilling the mind where the unbroken melody resounds.

dohas.title: Surati nirati man pavan palte...
dohas.fullText:
Surati nirati man pavan palte, banknaal sam keenjaye.
Sarbai phool asool addhasthar, ami mahaaras peenjaye || 14 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Let surati, nirati, mind and breath be reversed
Make them like the curved channel (bank naal)
All the flowers and roots
The great nectar-elixir

dohas.saralarth: Reverse surati, nirati, mind and breath, and make them like the curved channel. When all flowers and roots are stilled, drink the great nectar-elixir.
dohas.gahraBhav: The bank naal is the deep portion of the Sushumna. It is called 'bank' (crooked) because it does not rise straight up.

dohas.title: Sapt puri merudand khojo...
dohas.fullText:
Sapt puri merudand khojo, man mansa gah raakhiye.
Udhain bhanwar aakaash gamanoon, paanch pacheesaun naakhiye || 15 ||

shabdarth.meaning: The seven cities — the seven chakras
The spinal column — the path of the Sushumna
Hold the mind and its desires firmly
The five elements and the twenty-five categories of nature

dohas.saralarth: Seek the seven cities within the spinal column, and hold the mind and its desires firmly. Let the bee soar into the sky — cast off the five elements and the twenty-five categories of nature.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'The seven cities of the spinal column' — the seven chakras within the spine. To seek them is the practice of the Brahm-Vedi.

dohas.title: Gagan mandal ki sail kar le...
dohas.fullText:
Gagan mandal ki sail kar le, bahuri na aisa daav hai.
Chal hansa parlok pathaaun, bhau saagar nahin aav hai || 16 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Make the journey, take the tour
Such an opportunity will not come again
I shall send you to the world beyond
You will not return to the ocean of existence

dohas.saralarth: Make the journey to the sphere of the sky — such an opportunity will not come again. Move on, swan-soul, I shall send you to the world beyond — you will not return to the ocean of existence.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Such an opportunity will not come again' — this human life is a rare chance. The Guru shows the swan-soul the way to the world beyond.

dohas.title: Kandarp jeet udeet jogi...
dohas.fullText:
Kandarp jeet udeet jogi, shat karmi yauh khel hai.
Abhai maalni haar goonden, surati nirati ka mel hai || 17 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Conqueror of Kamadeva — victory over desire
Adept in the six practices
The fearless gardener-woman
Weaves a garland

dohas.saralarth: The awakened yogi who has conquered desire — this is the play of the six practices. The fearless gardener-woman weaves a garland — this is the union of surati and nirati.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Conqueror of desire' — only one who has conquered lust is a true yogi. The union of surati and nirati is that gardener's garland.

dohas.title: Sohang jaap ajaap tharpo...
dohas.fullText:
Sohang jaap ajaap tharpo, trikuti sanyam dhuni lagai.
Maan sarovar nhaan hansa, gangoo sahans mukh jit bagai || 18 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Establish, set firm
The melody of restraint at the Trikuti
Bathing in the Mansarovar lake
Where it flows from a thousand mouths

dohas.saralarth: Establish the unspoken recitation of Sohang — let the melody of restraint resound at the Trikuti. Let the swan-soul bathe in the Mansarovar, where the Ganga flows from a thousand mouths.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Establish the unspoken Sohang' — make the Sohang recitation your very nature. The Mansarovar symbolizes the pure soul.

dohas.title: Kaalindri kurbaan kaadar...
dohas.fullText:
Kaalindri kurbaan kaadar, anbigat moorati khoob hai.
Chhatra swet vishaal lochan, galtaana mahboob hai || 19 ||

shabdarth.meaning: The dark power (Kali shakti)
The imperceptible image
A white canopy and vast eyes
The beloved (Arabic)

dohas.saralarth: The dark power is offered up — the imperceptible image of the Almighty is beautiful. A white canopy and vast eyes — in Galtana he is the Beloved.
dohas.gahraBhav: Galtana is the sacred abode of Ganesh. The 'beloved' image of the Supreme Being — the highest sentiment of love.

dohas.title: Dil andar deedaar darshan...
dohas.fullText:
Dil andar deedaar darshan, baahar ant na jaaiye.
Kaaya maaya kahaan bapuri, tan man sheesh chadhaaiye || 20 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Vision within the heart
Do not wander outside
Wretched, petty
Offer up body, mind and head

dohas.saralarth: The vision comes within the heart — do not wander outside. Body and illusion are petty, wretched things — offer up body, mind and head.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Vision within the heart' — the vision of the Supreme Being is not outside but within. This is the message of both Vedanta and the Sufis.

dohas.title: Anbigat aadi jugaadi jogi...
dohas.fullText:
Anbigat aadi jugaadi jogi, sat purush lyauleen hai.
Gagan mandal galtaan gaibi, jaat ajaat bedeen hai || 21 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Imperceptible
From the beginning of the ages
Absorbed in love
Beyond caste and creed, without distinction

dohas.saralarth: The imperceptible Yogi, from the very beginning of the ages — the Sat Purush is absorbed in love. Unseen within the sphere of the sky — beyond caste and creed.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Beyond caste and creed' — the Supreme Being cannot be bound by any caste or religion.

dohas.title: Sukhsaagar ratnaagar nirbhay...
dohas.fullText:
Sukhsaagar ratnaagar nirbhay, nij mukhbaani gaavahin.
Jhin aakar ajokh nirmal, drishti mushti nahin aavahin || 22 ||

shabdarth.meaning: A mine of jewels
The utterance of his own mouth
Subtle in form and beyond compare
Comes neither into sight nor into the grasp

dohas.saralarth: An ocean of bliss, a mine of jewels and fearless — he sings with his own utterance. Subtle in form, pure and beyond compare — he comes neither into sight nor into the grasp.
dohas.gahraBhav: The Supreme Being can neither be seen nor grasped — yet he is experienced.

dohas.title: Jhil mil noor jahar joti...
dohas.fullText:
Jhil mil noor jahar joti, koti padma ujiyaar hai.
Ulat nain besunn bistar, jahaan-tahaan deedaar hai || 23 ||

shabdarth.meaning: The light of radiance made manifest
The brilliance of ten million lotuses
The inward gaze — the inner eye
Vision here and everywhere

dohas.saralarth: A shimmering light is made manifest — the brilliance of ten million lotuses. When the inner eye opens, upon the bed of the void there is vision here and everywhere.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'The inward eye' — when the outward-looking eyes turn inward, the Supreme Being is beheld.

dohas.title: Asht kamal dal sakal ramta...
dohas.fullText:
Asht kamal dal sakal ramta, trikuti kamal madhya nirakhahin.
Swet dhwaja sunn gumbad aage, pachrang jhande pharakahin || 24 ||

shabdarth.meaning: The eight-petalled lotus
Behold within the lotus of the Trikuti
Banners of five colours flutter

dohas.saralarth: The eight-petalled lotus pervades all — behold within the lotus of the Trikuti. Before the white banner and the dome of the void, banners of five colours flutter.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Banners of five colours' — symbols of the five elements. The dome of the void is that state where all colours become one.

dohas.title: Sunn mandal Satlok chaliye...
dohas.fullText:
Sunn mandal Satlok chaliye, nau dar mund bisunn hai.
Divya chisambon ek bimb dekhya, nij shravan suni dhuni hai || 25 ||

shabdarth.meaning: The realm of Truth — the supreme abode
The nine doors closed — the great void
With divine sight
Heard the melody with one's own ears

dohas.saralarth: Move toward the sphere of the void and Satlok — when the nine doors are closed, there is the great void. With divine sight one beheld a single image and with one's own ears heard the melody.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'The nine doors closed' — when the nine sense-gates are shut, a single image within is revealed.

dohas.title: Charan kamal mein hans rahte...
dohas.fullText:
Charan kamal mein hans rahte, bahurangi bariyaam hain.
Sookshm moorati Shyaam soorati, achal abhangi Raam hain || 26 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Many-hued and mighty
Subtle form and dark visage
The unmoving, unbroken Ram

dohas.saralarth: In the lotus of the feet the swan-souls abide — many-hued and mighty. Subtle form, dark visage — the unmoving and unbroken Ram.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'The swan in the lotus-feet' — the soul rests at the feet of the Supreme Being — this is liberation.

dohas.title: Nau sur bandh nisank khelo...
dohas.fullText:
Nau sur bandh nisank khelo, dasmen dar mukhmool hai.
Maali na koop anoop sajni, bin beli ka phool hai || 27 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Closing the nine senses
The tenth door — the Brahmarandhra, the source
A flower without a vine — bloomed of itself

dohas.saralarth: Close the nine senses and play without fear — the tenth door, the Brahmarandhra, is the source. Without gardener, without well — it is a flower bloomed of itself without a vine.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'The tenth door' — the Brahmarandhra, through which the soul merges into the Supreme Being. 'A flower without a vine' — a spontaneous, self-arising experience.

dohas.title: Swaans uswaans pavan koon paltai...
dohas.fullText:
Swaans uswaans pavan koon paltai, naag phuni koon bhoonch hai.
Surati nirati ka baandh beda, gagan mandal koon koonch hai || 28 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Inhalation and exhalation
Press down the serpent's hood — the kundalini
A raft — a boat
Departure — the setting forth

dohas.saralarth: Reverse the inward and outward breath and press down the serpent's hood (the kundalini). Bind the raft of surati and nirati — the journey is toward the sphere of the sky.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'The serpent's hood' is the kundalini power. To awaken it and carry it upward is the essence of the practice.

dohas.title: Sun le jog vijog hansa...
dohas.fullText:
Sun le jog vijog hansa, shabd mahal koon siddh karo.
Yoh gurugyaan vigyaan baani, jeevat hi jag mein maro || 29 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Union and separation — meeting and parting
The palace of the Word — the supreme abode
Die while yet alive in the world — become liberated-while-living

dohas.saralarth: Listen, swan-soul, to union and separation, and master the palace of the Word. This is the utterance of the Guru's knowledge and realization — die while yet alive in the world.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Die while yet alive in the world' — the message of liberation-while-living. Let the ego die, not the body — this is the living death.

dohas.title: Ujal hirambar swet bhaunra...
dohas.fullText:
Ujal hirambar swet bhaunra, akshay vriksh sat baag hai.
Jeeto kaal visaal Sohang, tar teevar bairaag hai || 30 ||

shabdarth.meaning: A white bee — an auspicious symbol
The imperishable tree and the garden of Truth
The bank of intense, deep dispassion

dohas.saralarth: In the luminous sky is a white bee, the imperishable tree and the garden of Truth. Conquer Time through Sohang — this is the bank of intense dispassion.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'The imperishable tree' — that tree of knowledge which is never destroyed. 'The bank of intense dispassion' — the shore of the river of dispassion.

dohas.title: Mansa naari kar panihaari...
dohas.fullText:
Mansa naari kar panihaari, khaakhi man jahaan maaliya.
Kubhank kaaya baag lagaaya, phoole hain phool visaaliya || 31 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Make the desiring will a water-bearer
The mind held in check — the disciplined mind
Through kumbhak the body's garden was planted

dohas.saralarth: Make the desiring will a water-bearer and hold the mind in check. Through kumbhak the garden of the body was planted — vast flowers have bloomed.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Desire as water-bearer' — make desire the servant of practice, not its master. Through kumbhak, flowers bloom in the garden of the body.

dohas.title: Kachh machh koormbh dhauloon...
dohas.fullText:
Kachh machh koormbh dhauloon, shesh sahans phun gaavahin.
Naarad muni se rahain nishdin, Brahma paar na paavahin || 32 ||

shabdarth.meaning: The tortoise, fish and turtle — incarnations of Vishnu
The thousand hoods of Sheshnaga
Sages such as Narada
Even Brahma cannot find his limit

dohas.saralarth: The tortoise, fish and turtle — the thousand hoods of Sheshnaga all sing of him. Sages like Narada remain day and night — yet even Brahma cannot find his limit.
dohas.gahraBhav: Even Brahma cannot measure the glory of the Supreme Being — a depiction of his boundlessness.

dohas.title: Shambhu jog bijog saadhya...
dohas.fullText:
Shambhu jog bijog saadhya, achal adig samaadh hai.
Anbigat ki gati naahin jaani, leela agam agaadh hai || 33 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Shambhu — Shiva
Unmoving, unshakeable absorption (samadhi)
The course of the imperceptible Supreme

dohas.saralarth: Shiva mastered union and separation — an unmoving, unshakeable samadhi. The course of the imperceptible One was not known — his play is unreachable and unfathomable.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Shiva mastered union and separation' — Shiva himself is a practitioner of yoga. Even Shiva could not know the play of the Supreme Being.

dohas.title: Sanakaadik aur siddh chauraasi...
dohas.fullText:
Sanakaadik aur siddh chauraasi, dhyaan dharat hain taas ka.
Chaubeesaun avataar japat hain, param hans prakaas ka || 34 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Sanak, Sanandan, Sanatan and Sanatkumar — sons of Brahma
The eighty-four adepts
The twenty-four incarnations
The light of the supreme swan

dohas.saralarth: The Sanakas and the eighty-four adepts meditate upon him. The twenty-four incarnations recite the light of the supreme swan.
dohas.gahraBhav: Even the twenty-four incarnations worship the supreme swan — such is the supremacy of that Supreme Power.

dohas.title: Sahans athaasi aur taiteeson...
dohas.fullText:
Sahans athaasi aur taiteeson, sooraj chand chiraag hain.
Dhar ambar dharni dhar rahte, anbigat achal bihaag hain || 35 ||

shabdarth.meaning: The eighty-eight thousand sages
The sun, the moon and the lamp
Earth, sky and ground
Imperceptible, unmoving, the Bihag raga

dohas.saralarth: The eighty-eight thousand and the thirty-three crore — the sun, moon and lamp. Dwelling within earth and sky, he is imperceptible, unmoving, the Bihag melody.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Bihag' is a raga sung in the middle of the night. The Supreme Being is that unmoving music.

dohas.title: Sur nar munijan siddh aur saadhik...
dohas.fullText:
Sur nar munijan siddh aur saadhik, paar Brahm koon rahat hain.
Ghar ghar mangalaachaar chauri, gyaan jog jahaan bahat hain || 36 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Seekers, practitioners
Abide in the supreme Brahman
The seat of auspicious rites
Where the yoga of knowledge flows

dohas.saralarth: Gods, humans, sages, adepts and seekers — all abide in the supreme Brahman. In every home is the seat of auspicious rites, where the yoga of knowledge flows.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Auspicious rites in every home' — where there is the yoga of knowledge, every home is filled with auspiciousness.

dohas.title: Chitra Gupt Dharm Raay gaavain...
dohas.fullText:
Chitra Gupt Dharm Raay gaavain, aadi maaya Onkaar hai.
Koti Saraswati laap karat hain, aisa Paarbrahm darbaar hai || 37 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Chitragupta — the recorder of deeds
Primal illusion in the form of Onkar
Ten million goddesses Saraswati
Sing and offer praise

dohas.saralarth: Chitragupta and Dharmaraja sing — the primal illusion is in the form of Onkar. Ten million Saraswatis offer praise — such is the court of the supreme Brahman.
dohas.gahraBhav: The court of the supreme Brahman — where even the deities of Time sing. This is a glimpse of the supreme kingdom.

dohas.title: Kaamdhenu kalpvriksh jaakain...
dohas.fullText:
Kaamdhenu kalpvriksh jaakain, Indra anant sur bharat hain.
Paarvati kar jor Lakshmi, Saavitri shobha karat hain || 38 ||

shabdarth.meaning: The wish-fulfilling cow and the wish-fulfilling tree
Indra and countless gods serve
With folded hands

dohas.saralarth: At whose court are the wish-fulfilling cow and tree, where Indra and countless gods attend. Parvati, Lakshmi and Savitri with folded hands lend their splendour.
dohas.gahraBhav: A depiction of the abundance of the supreme abode — there every wish is fulfilled.

dohas.title: Gandharv gyaani aur muni dhyaani...
dohas.fullText:
Gandharv gyaani aur muni dhyaani, paanchon tatva khavaas hain.
Trigun teen bahurang baaji, koi jan birle daas hain || 39 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Gandharvas — the celestial musicians
The five elements are his attendants
The many-hued play of the three qualities
Rare devotees

dohas.saralarth: Wise gandharvas and meditating sages — the five elements are his attendants. The many-hued play of the three qualities — rare are the souls who become his servants.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'The five elements are his attendants' — they serve that Supreme Power. 'Rare servants' — the true devotee is rare.

dohas.title: Dhruv Prahlaad agaadh ag hai...
dohas.fullText:
Dhruv Prahlaad agaadh ag hai, Janak Videhi jor hai.
Chale vimaan nidaan beetya, Dharmraaj ki bandh taur hain || 40 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Dhruva and Prahlada — great devotees
King Janaka — the bodiless one (Videha)
Upon a divine vehicle at the end
Freed from the bondage of Dharmaraja

dohas.saralarth: Dhruva and Prahlada — unfathomable great ones; Janaka the Videha. All in the end ascended the divine vehicle — freed from the bondage of Dharmaraja.
dohas.gahraBhav: The example of the great devotees — all were liberated in the end. 'Freed from the bondage of Dharmaraja' means liberation.

dohas.title: Gorakh Datt jugaadi jogi...
dohas.fullText:
Gorakh Datt jugaadi jogi, naam Jalandhar leenjaye.
Bharthari Gopi Chanda seejhe, aisi deeksha deenjaye || 41 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Gorakhnath and Dattatreya — yogis of the ages
Jalandharnath
Bhartrihari and Gopichand
Were perfected, attained liberation

dohas.saralarth: Gorakhnath, Dattatreya, Jalandharnath — yogis of the ages. Bhartrihari and Gopichand were perfected — grant me such an initiation.
dohas.gahraBhav: Remembrance of the great seekers of the Nath tradition. 'Grant me such an initiation' — they pray for an initiation like theirs.

dohas.title: Sultaani Baajeed Fareeda...
dohas.fullText:
Sultaani Baajeed Fareeda, Peepa parche paaiya.
Deval pherya gop gosaain, Naama ki chhaan chhivaaiya || 42 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Sultan Bahu, Bayazid and Farid — Sufi saints
Pipaji gained recognition (of the truth)
Had Namdev's roof thatched

dohas.saralarth: Sultan Bahu, Bayazid, Farid and Pipaji — all gained the realization. He turned the temple about, the cowherd-lord, and thatched Namdev's roof.
dohas.gahraBhav: Saints of both the Hindu and Muslim traditions are remembered together — all devotees of the one Supreme Reality.

dohas.title: Chhaan chhivaai gau jivaai...
dohas.fullText:
Chhaan chhivaai gau jivaai, ganika chadhi vimaan mein.
Sadna bakre koon mat maarai, pahunche aan nidaan mein || 43 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Brought a cow back to life — worked a miracle
The courtesan ascended the divine vehicle — was liberated
Sadna the butcher — a devotee
In the end, in liberation

dohas.saralarth: He thatched the roof, revived the cow, and the courtesan ascended the divine vehicle. Sadna was stopped from slaying the goat — all in the end reached liberation.
dohas.gahraBhav: Even a courtesan attained liberation — in the grace of the Satguru there is no distinction. Even the lowest of the low can cross over.

dohas.title: Ajaamel se adham udhaare...
dohas.fullText:
Ajaamel se adham udhaare, patit paavan birad taas hai.
Kesho aan bhaya banjaara, shat dal keeni haas hai || 44 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Ajamil — a fallen soul
The vow of purifying the fallen
Keshav (Vishnu) came as a peddler
The smile of the six petals — the six chakras blossomed

dohas.saralarth: He delivered fallen ones like Ajamil — his vow is 'purifier of the fallen'. Keshav came as a peddler — the smile of the six petals (the awakening of the six chakras).
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Purifier of the fallen' — however fallen one may be, the Supreme Being delivers. 'The smile of the six petals' — the awakening of the chakras is liberation.

dohas.title: Dhana bhagat ka khet nipaaya...
dohas.fullText:
Dhana bhagat ka khet nipaaya, Maadho dai siklaat hai.
Panda paanv bujhaaya Satguru, Jagannaath ki baat hai || 45 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Tilled the field — ploughed it
Madhav lent his lustre
Eased the priest's foot — a miracle

dohas.saralarth: He sowed the field of Dhana the devotee — Madhav lent his lustre. The Satguru eased the priest's foot — this is the tale of Jagannath.
dohas.gahraBhav: The story of Dhana the devotee — the Supreme Being himself does the devotee's work.

dohas.title: Bhaddhi het Kesho banjaara...
dohas.fullText:
Bhaddhi het Kesho banjaara, sang Raidaas Kamaal the.
He har he har hoti aai, gun chhai aur paal the || 46 ||

shabdarth.meaning: For the sake of devotion
Keshav came as a peddler
Saint Raidas and Kamal (Kabir's son)
The call of the name of Hari

dohas.saralarth: For devotion's sake Keshav became a peddler — with him were Raidas and Kamal. The call of 'He Har, He Har' kept rising — a heritage of virtue to be cherished.
dohas.gahraBhav: Raidas and Kamal in the lineage of saints — all are strung upon the single thread of devotion.

dohas.title: Gaibi khyaal visaal Satguru...
dohas.fullText:
Gaibi khyaal visaal Satguru, achal digambar theer hain.
Bhaddhi het aan kaaya dhar aaye, anbigat sat Kabir hain || 47 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Contemplation of the unseen (ghaib)
Unmoving and sky-clad — the naked truth
Came taking on a body for the sake of devotion

dohas.saralarth: The Satguru of the vast contemplation of the unseen — unmoving and sky-clad. For devotion's sake he came taking on a body — he is the imperceptible Truth, Kabir.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'The imperceptible Truth, Kabir' — Kabir Sahib is the imperceptible supreme Truth. He came taking on a body for the sake of devotion.

dohas.title: Naanak daad agam agaadh...
dohas.fullText:
Naanak daad agam agaadh, teri jahaaj khevat sahi.
Sukh saagar ke hans aaye, bhaddhi hirambar ur dhari || 48 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Praise of Guru Nanak
The boatman of the ship is true
The sky of devotion

dohas.saralarth: Guru Nanak — unreachable and unfathomable; the boatman of your ship is true. The swans of the ocean of bliss came — holding the sky of devotion within the heart.
dohas.gahraBhav: Garibdas Ji bows even to Guru Nanak. This is the spirit of harmony among all faiths.

dohas.title: Koti bhaanu prakaash poorn...
dohas.fullText:
Koti bhaanu prakaash poorn, room room ki laar hai.
Achal abhangi hai satsangi, anbigat ka deedaar hai || 49 ||

shabdarth.meaning: The light of ten million suns
Attachment in every pore
Unmoving and unbroken
Vision of the imperceptible One

dohas.saralarth: The light of ten million suns — attachment in every pore. Unmoving, unbroken, a true companion — the vision of the imperceptible One.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'The light of ten million suns' — the Supreme Being's light surpasses ten million suns. 'Attachment in every pore' — all-pervading love.

dohas.title: Dhan Satguru updesh deva...
dohas.fullText:
Dhan Satguru updesh deva, chauraasi bhram metahin.
Tej punj aan deh dhar kar, is vidhi ham koon bhentahin || 50 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Blessed is the Satguru
Erases the delusion of the 8.4 million births

shabdarth.word: tej punj aan deh dhar kar
shabdarth.meaning: Came taking on a body in the form of a mass of light
In this way he meets us

dohas.saralarth: Blessed is the teaching of the Satguru, who erases the delusion of the 8.4 million births. Taking on a body as a mass of light, in this way he meets us.
dohas.gahraBhav: The Satguru is a 'mass of light' — he is light in form. Taking on a body is his voluntary grace.

dohas.title: Shabd nivaas aakaashvaani...
dohas.fullText:
Shabd nivaas aakaashvaani, yoh Satguru ka rup hai.
Chand sooraj na pavan na paani, na jahaan chhaaya dhoop hai || 51 ||

shabdarth.meaning: The dwelling of the Word, the celestial voice
The duality of shade and sun

dohas.saralarth: The dwelling of the Word, the celestial voice — this is the form of the Satguru. There is neither moon nor sun, neither wind nor water, neither shade nor sun.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'The dwelling of the Word, the celestial voice' — the Satguru is the Word-Brahman. Where the dualities of nature are absent — that is the supreme realm.

dohas.title: Rahta ramta Raam Sahib...
dohas.fullText:
Rahta ramta Raam Sahib, avgat Alah alekh hai.
Bhoole panth bibhraant vaadi, kul ka khaavind ek hai || 52 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Ram who dwells and pervades everywhere
Imperceptible, Allah (Arabic), the unwritten
The strayed and deluded disputants
The Lord of all creation

dohas.saralarth: Ram the Sahib dwells and pervades everywhere — imperceptible, Allah and the unwritten. The strayed and deluded disputants — the Lord of all creation is one.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Imperceptible, Allah, the unwritten' — one Supreme Being in Hindi, Arabic and Sanskrit alike. This is the oneness of all faiths.

dohas.title: Room room mein jaap jap le...
dohas.fullText:
Room room mein jaap jap le, asht kamal dal mel hai.
Surati nirati koon kamal pathvo, jahaan deepak bin tel hai || 53 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Recite in every pore
The union of the eight-petalled lotus
A lamp without oil — self-luminous

dohas.saralarth: Recite the Name in every pore — there is the union of the eight-petalled lotus. Send surati and nirati to the lotus where a lamp burns without oil.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'A lamp without oil' — that inner light which burns by no external fuel. This is the self-luminous Supreme Being.

dohas.title: Hardam khoj hanoj haajar...
dohas.fullText:
Hardam khoj hanoj haajar, Triveni ke teer hain.
Daas Garib tabeeb Satguru, bandi chhod Kabir hain || 54 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Search at every moment
Present even now
Physician, healer (Arabic)
Kabir, the liberator of captives

dohas.saralarth: Search at every moment — he is present even now, upon the bank of the Triveni. The Satguru, physician of the servant Garib, is Kabir, the liberator of captives.
dohas.gahraBhav: The close of the Brahm-Vedi. 'Kabir the liberator of captives' — the very identity of Kabir Sahib. 'Tabeeb' — the physician of the soul's ailments.

dohas.title: Niranjan-Niranjan-Niranjan niraakaar...
dohas.fullText:
Niranjan-Niranjan-Niranjan niraakaar bhaj re.
Taata na seera, raata na peera, dharo dhyaan dheera.
Rahya aap thir re adoloon aboloon achhedoon abhedoon, pare sain parain rai.
Kaho kaun here, agam athaah dariya, gaya toon bisar rai.
Bina mool mola, jo kaala na dhola.
Surati sindh sailoon, karo door phailoon.
Bhajo kyon na Hari re.
Pashu toon patangam bhuvangam bisaasi, dai deh nar re.
Raho Raam ramta rakho sheela samta, kare tohi ajar re.
Alakh noor mela guru kaun chela, bajar kaal dar re.
Shabd mein samaana amaana ajokhoon, chalo kyon na ghar re.
Mool mantra gauhraaya bhed kinhe birle jan paaya.
Pind brahmand sain sindh nyaari, kuchh aisi hi dhaaran dhaari.
Dil andar deedaar, nahin vaar paar bajar paul pat.
Kholhanhi tol mol.
Shabd sindhu jhalkai, daas Garib nij noor palkai ||

shabdarth.meaning: The taintless and formless Supreme Being
Neither hot nor cold — beyond duality
Neither red nor yellow — beyond colour
Unshakeable, unspeakable, uncleavable and impenetrable
Beyond even the beyond
Root and Master — the foundation and the Lord
Journey across the ocean of consciousness
Moth and serpent — lowly creatures
Virtue and equanimity
Free of decay — immortal
The light of the Unseen was met
Immeasurable and beyond compare
Deepened — went down into the depths
The adamantine gate-doors
One's own light shimmers in a flash

dohas.saralarth: Recite the taintless, formless Niranjan. He is neither hot nor cold, neither red nor yellow — beyond all duality. He is unshakeable, unspeakable, uncleavable and impenetrable — beyond even the beyond. Who can find him? He is the unreachable, fathomless river — and you have forgotten him. The Master without root — neither black nor white. Journey across the ocean of consciousness — why not recite the Name of Hari? You have been a moth, a serpent and a fool, yet you have been given a human body. Abide in Ram, keep virtue and equanimity — that makes you immortal. The light of the Unseen was met — the Guru himself is the disciple. The immeasurable and incomparable is contained within the Word — why not return home? The root-mantra runs deep — rare are those who found its secret. The ocean is distinct from body and cosmos; such is the practice held. The vision is within the heart, with no near or far, behind the adamantine gate. Its worth is beyond all measure. The ocean of the Word shimmers — and the servant Garib's own light flashes forth.
dohas.gahraBhav: This is the essence of the Mool-Mantra Granth. Each line describes various qualities of the Supreme Being and various facets of spiritual practice. 'The root-mantra runs deep' — this mantra has gone into the depths; it is not mere words but experience. 'The servant Garib's own light flashes forth' — within Garibdas Ji's soul the light of the Supreme Being shimmers — this is the supreme fruit of practice.

dohas.title: Uttam kul kartaar de...
dohas.fullText:
Garib uttam kul kartaar de, dwaadas bhooshan sang.
Roop dravya de daya kar, gyaan bhajan satsang || 1 ||

shabdarth.meaning: The maker of a noble lineage
The twelve ornaments — the twelve virtues
Beauty and wealth

dohas.saralarth: The Supreme Being grants a noble lineage, and beauty and wealth together with the twelve virtues. He also grants knowledge, devotion and holy company.
dohas.gahraBhav: To the true seeker the Supreme Being grants both material and spiritual riches.

dohas.title: Seel santosh vivek de...
dohas.fullText:
Seel santosh vivek de, kshama daya iktaar.
Bhaav bhaddhi vairaag de, naam niraalambh saar || 2 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Virtue, contentment and discernment
Steady, unbroken
The supportless Name is the very essence

dohas.saralarth: Grant virtue, contentment, discernment, forgiveness and compassion in steady measure. Grant feeling, devotion and dispassion — the supportless Name is the essence of all.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'The supportless Name' — to rest upon the Name of the Supreme Being alone, without any other prop.

dohas.title: Jog yukti swaasthya Jagdeesh de...
dohas.fullText:
Jog yukti swaasthya Jagdeesh de, sookshm dhyaan dayaal.
Akal akeen ajanm jati, athsiddhi naunidhi khyaal || 3 ||

shabdarth.meaning: The techniques of yoga
Subtle meditation, the finest concentration
The eight powers and the nine treasures

dohas.saralarth: O Jagdish! Grant the techniques of yoga, good health and subtle meditation. Grant the state of the partless, the steadfast, the unborn and the celibate, and the contemplation of the eight powers and nine treasures.
dohas.gahraBhav: A prayer to the Supreme Being for the whole of spiritual attainment. The eight powers and nine treasures — both material and spiritual abundance.

dohas.title: Swarg narak baanchai nahin...
dohas.fullText:
Swarg narak baanchai nahin, moksh bandhan sain door.
Badi gareebi jagat mein, sant charan raj dhoor || 4 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Has no concern for
Even liberation is far from bondage
The dust of the feet

dohas.saralarth: He has no concern for heaven or hell, and even liberation lies beyond bondage. The greatest humility in the world is to receive the dust of a saint's feet.
dohas.gahraBhav: To rise above all desires — heaven, hell and even liberation — and to ask only for the dust of a saint's feet is true humility.

dohas.title: Jeevat mukta so kaho...
dohas.fullText:
Jeevat mukta so kaho, aasha trishna khand.
Man ke jeete jeet hai, kyon bharmen brahmand || 5 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Liberated while living
The destruction of hope and craving
To conquer the mind is the only victory

dohas.saralarth: Call him liberated-while-living who has destroyed hope and craving. To conquer the mind is the only victory — why wander through the cosmos?
dohas.gahraBhav: Liberation in this very life. 'To conquer the mind is victory' — winning the inner battle is greater than winning all others.

dohas.title: Saala karm shareer mein...
dohas.fullText:
Saala karm shareer mein, Satguru diya lakhaay.
Garibdaas galtaan pad, nahin aavai nahin jaay || 6 ||

shabdarth.meaning: The lesson of the school — the schooling of life
The supreme state of Galta
Free of coming and going

dohas.saralarth: The Satguru revealed the schooling of life within this body. Garibdas — that supreme state of Galta where there is no coming and going.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'The state of Galta' — that supreme station which is beyond birth and death.

dohas.title: Chauraasi ki chaal kya...
dohas.fullText:
Chauraasi ki chaal kya, mo seti sun leh.
Chori jaari karat hain, jaakai munhde kheh || 7 ||

shabdarth.meaning: The course of the 8.4 million births
Hear it from me
Ash upon the face — disgrace and downfall

dohas.saralarth: What is the course of the 8.4 million births — hear it from me. Those who commit theft and adultery (sin) — ash falls upon their faces.
dohas.gahraBhav: The consequence of sinful deeds is to wander through the cycle of 8.4 million births.

dohas.title: Kaam krodh mad lobh lat...
dohas.fullText:
Kaam krodh mad lobh lat, chhuti rahe vikraal.
Krodh kasaai ur basai, kushabd chhura ghar ghaal || 8 ||

shabdarth.meaning: The five vices — lust, anger, pride, greed and craving
Anger, the butcher, dwells in the heart
Harsh words wound like a dagger within the home

dohas.saralarth: Lust, anger, pride, greed and craving are terrible vices. Anger, the butcher, dwells in the heart, and harsh words wound like a dagger.
dohas.gahraBhav: The five vices are the seeker's greatest enemies. 'Harsh words like a dagger' — the misuse of speech inflicts the deepest wound.

dohas.title: Harsh shok hai shvaan gati...
dohas.fullText:
Harsh shog hai shvaan gati, sanshay sarp shareer.
Raag dvesh bade rog hain, jam ke pade janjeer || 9 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Joy and grief — the restless gait of a dog
Doubt, a serpent within the body
Attachment and aversion are great diseases

dohas.saralarth: Joy and grief are like the restless gait of a dog, and doubt is like a serpent in the body. Attachment and aversion are great diseases that bind one in the chains of Yama.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Attachment and aversion are great diseases' — these keep one bound in the cycle of birth and death.

dohas.title: Aasha trishna nadi mein...
dohas.fullText:
Aasha trishna nadi mein, doobe teenon lok.
Mansa maaya vistari, aatm aatm dosh || 10 ||

shabdarth.meaning: The river of hope and craving
The desires of the mind and illusion spread wide
The flaw of the soul

dohas.saralarth: In the river of hope and craving all three worlds are drowned. The mind's desires and illusion have spread wide — this is the flaw of the soul.
dohas.gahraBhav: Hope and craving form the deepest river. 'The flaw of the soul' — recognizing one's own weakness is the first step of practice.

dohas.title: Ek shatru ek mitra hain...
dohas.fullText:
Ek shatru ek mitra hain, bhool padi re praan.
Jam ki nagri jaayega, shabd hamaara maan || 11 ||

shabdarth.meaning: One enemy (illusion-mind), one friend (the Supreme Being)
You will go to the city of Yama — death is certain

dohas.saralarth: There is one enemy and one friend — the soul has forgotten this. Accept our word — you will have to go to the city of Yama.
dohas.gahraBhav: One enemy is the illusion-mind; one friend is the Guru and the Supreme Being. To know this is life's greatest understanding.

dohas.title: Nindya bindya chhod de...
dohas.fullText:
Nindya bindya chhod de, santan son kar preet.
Bhausaagar tir jaat hai, jeevat mukt ateet || 12 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Slander and backbiting
Liberated-while-living and beyond Time

dohas.saralarth: Give up slander and backbiting, and form love for the saints. One crosses the ocean of existence — liberated-while-living and beyond Time.
dohas.gahraBhav: Giving up slander and forming love for saints — two simple yet great spiritual practices.

dohas.title: Je tere upjai nahin...
dohas.fullText:
Je tere upjai nahin, to shabd saakhi sun leh.
Saakhi bhoot sangeet hain, jaasain laavo neh || 13 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Does not arise of itself
The sakhi is the music of the past (the bygone)

dohas.saralarth: If it does not arise of itself, then listen to the witness of the Word (the sakhi). The sakhi is the music of the bygone — form love with it.
dohas.gahraBhav: Even when self-experience does not arise, the witness of the Word shows the way.

dohas.title: Swarg saat asmaan par...
dohas.fullText:
Swarg saat asmaan par, bhatkat hai man moodh.
Khaalik to khoya nahin, isi mahal mein dhoondh || 14 ||

shabdarth.meaning: The seven skies
The ignorant mind
The Creator, the Supreme Being (Arabic)
Search within

dohas.saralarth: The ignorant mind searches across the seven skies. The Creator has gone nowhere — search within this very palace (your own self).
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Search within this palace' — this body is the palace of the Supreme Being.

dohas.title: Karm bharm bhaari lage...
dohas.fullText:
Karm bharm bhaari lage, sansa sool bambool.
Daali paano dolte, parsat naahin mool || 15 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Doubt like the thorns of an acacia
Branches and leaves sway
They do not touch the root

dohas.saralarth: Karma and delusion weigh heavily — doubt is a thorny acacia. The branches and leaves sway, but they do not touch the root.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'They do not touch the root' — outward practices do not reach the root. To touch the root one must go within.

dohas.title: Swaasa hi mein saar pad...
dohas.fullText:
Swaasa hi mein saar pad, pad mein swaasa saar.
Dam dehi ka khoj kar, aavaagaman nivaar || 16 ||

shabdarth.meaning: The essential state lies within the breath itself
Investigate the breath and the body

dohas.saralarth: The essential state lies within the breath, and within that state lies the essence of breath. Investigate breath and body — and end the round of coming and going.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'The essential state within the breath' — the breath itself is the recitation of Sohang. To know this is liberation from the cycle of birth and death.

dohas.title: Bin Satguru paavai nahin...
dohas.fullText:
Bin Satguru paavai nahin khaalik khoj vichaar.
Chauraasi jag jaat hai, chinhat naahin saar || 17 ||

shabdarth.meaning: The search for and contemplation of the Creator
Does not recognize the essence

dohas.saralarth: Without the Satguru the search for the Creator does not succeed. The world goes through the 8.4 million births — it does not recognize the essence.
dohas.gahraBhav: Without a Guru the search for the Supreme Being is impossible. 'The essence' — that root of the soul which is the Supreme Being.

dohas.title: Mard gard mein mil gaye...
dohas.fullText:
Mard gard mein mil gaye, Raavan se randheer.
Kans ke shoor Chaanoor se, Hirnaakush balbeer || 18 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Mighty men crumbled into dust
Warriors like Ravana
Mighty ones like Hiranyakashipu

dohas.saralarth: Warriors like Ravana, mighty fighters of Kamsa like Chanura, and strong ones like Hiranyakashipu — all crumbled into dust.
dohas.gahraBhav: Even the mightiest are mortal. 'Mighty men crumbled into dust' — strength and prowess in battle do not save one from death.

dohas.title: Teri kya buniyaad hai...
dohas.fullText:
Teri kya buniyaad hai, jeev janm dhar let.
Garibdaas Hari naam bin, khaali parsi khet || 19 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Foundation, basis
The soul keeps taking birth
An empty, barren field

dohas.saralarth: What is your foundation? The soul keeps taking birth. Garibdas — without the Name of Hari the field (of life) lies empty and barren.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'An empty, barren field' — without the Name of Hari, life is like a field left unploughed and unsown. In the end, empty.

dohas.title: Ugmant sooroon...
dohas.fullText:
Ugmant sooroon, varshant nooroon, baajant tooroon,
sakal lok bharpooroon, kaal koon thar dooroon.
Sat sukrit Shri Sooraj baala, jap tap sanyam ke rakhvaala.
Haath khadag gal pauhap ki maala kaanon kundal roop vishaala.
Riddhi siddhi deejo kar prati paala, moksh mukti ke tum hi dayaala.
Ham par Sooraj kar kripaala. Daas Garib chintaavan vaala ||

shabdarth.meaning: To the rising sun
Raining down radiance (light)
Sounding the trumpet
Filling all the worlds
Driving away Time (darkness)
Doer of good and true deeds
A garland of flowers
Grant prosperity and powers
Like the wish-stone — remover of all cares

dohas.saralarth: Salutation to the rising sun — who rains down radiance, sounds the trumpet, fills all the worlds and drives away Time. The true and virtuous Lord Sun — guardian of recitation, austerity and restraint. With a sword in hand, a garland of flowers about the neck and rings in the ears — a vast form. Grant prosperity and powers, gracious giver of liberation — show us your grace. The servant Garib prays to him who, like the wish-stone, removes all cares.
dohas.gahraBhav: The Surya Gayatri — a hymn of praise to the Sun-god. The sun is a symbol of knowledge, energy and life. 'Driving away Time' — in the sun's light, darkness (Time) is dispelled. This Gayatri is a prayer not only to the physical sun but also to the inner light of knowledge.

dohas.title: Om-Om-Om-Om...
dohas.fullText:
Om-Om-Om-Om, Kiliyoon-Kiliyoon-Kiliyoon-Kiliyoon.
Hariyoon-Hariyoon-Hariyoon-Hariyoon, Shriyoon-Shriyoon-Shriyoon-Shriyoon.
Sohoon-Sohoon-Sohoon-Sohoon, Satyoon-Satyoon-Satyoon-Satyoon.
Abhay pad Gayatri pathal pathante, arth dharm kaam moksh poorn phal labhte ||

shabdarth.meaning: Kleem — the seed-mantra of the power of Ganesh
Hreem — the seed-mantra of Vishnu
Shreem — the seed-mantra of Lakshmi
Sohang — 'That I am' — the realization of non-duality
Satyam — the supreme Truth
The Gayatri of the fearless state
Those who recite and impart it
The four aims of human life
Are obtained

dohas.saralarth: Om, Kleem, Hreem, Shreem, Sohang, Satyam — these seed-mantras recited four times each. Those who recite and impart this Gayatri of the fearless state obtain in full the four aims of life — wealth, righteousness, fulfilment and liberation.
dohas.gahraBhav: The Brahm Gayatri — a gathering of six seed-mantras. Om (the supreme Brahman), Kleem (power), Hreem (sustenance), Shreem (prosperity), Sohang (self-realization), Satyam (supreme Truth) — their recitation awakens the six chakras. 'The fearless state' — that condition in which there is fear of nothing.

dohas.title: Praan apaan samaanaadoon...
dohas.fullText:
Praan apaan samaanaadoon, man indri phal addhisthroon.
Naasaagre niraaloomboon, cheenhte dwaadas daloon.
Agar moole na moochha, moochha suh jeev janmoon.
Jeev janmoon suh bhram bhoote, bhram bhoote suh karm kaaloon.
Karm kaaloon suh vinaasti.
Har-har-har uchaar, Shiv yogi ki gati apaar.
Mahaadev Kailaash kunj, sur-nar munijan, sir karain punj.
Daas Garib dhar Shiv ka dhyaan bhaddhi mukti jin deenhin daan ||

shabdarth.meaning: Prana, Apana and Samana — three principal vital airs
Steady the mind and the senses
Supportless meditation upon the tip of the nose
The twelve-petalled one — the Anahata chakra
From stupor the soul takes birth
From delusion arise karma and Time
Destruction
Utterance — recitation
Worship — they bow
He who gave devotion and liberation in charity

dohas.saralarth: Master Prana, Apana and Samana — steady the mind and the senses. Meditate supportlessly upon the tip of the nose, and recognize the twelve petals. Without the root-tip comes stupor — from stupor the soul takes birth, from birth comes delusion, from delusion karma and Time, and from karma and Time comes destruction. Utter 'Har-Har-Har' — the way of the Shiva-yogi is boundless. Mahadev in the bower of Kailash — gods, humans and sages all bow before him. The servant Garib meditates upon Shiva, who gave devotion and liberation as a gift.
dohas.gahraBhav: The Geeta Gayatri — a synthesis of the yogic principles of the Gita with the meditation on Shiva. 'From stupor the soul takes birth' — ignorance (stupor) is the cause of rebirth. To understand this chain and break it is the message of the Gita.

dohas.title: Saaton vaar samool bakhaano...
dohas.fullText: Saaton vaar samool bakhaanoon, pahar ghadi pal jyotish jaano || 1 ||

shabdarth.meaning: The seven days — Monday through Sunday
Describe with their root
The pahar, ghadi and pal — divisions of time
The knowledge of astrology

dohas.saralarth: Know the seven days together with their root — know the astrology of the pahar, the ghadi and the pal.
dohas.gahraBhav: The Ramaini of the seven days — the relation between time and spiritual practice. Each day is linked to a particular practice and a particular planet.

dohas.title: Aitvaar antar nahin koi...
dohas.fullText: Aitvaar antar nahin koi, lagi chaanchari pad mein soi || 2 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Sunday — the day of the Sun
There is no difference
Chanchari — a kind of music

dohas.saralarth: On Sunday there is no difference at all — in that state the chanchari melody resounds.
dohas.gahraBhav: Sunday — the day of the Sun. 'Chanchari' is that sweet music which plays of itself within the soul.

dohas.title: Som sambhaal karo din raati...
dohas.fullText: Som sambhaal karo din raati, door karo nain dil ki kaanti || 3 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Monday — the day of the Moon
Take heed, keep watch
The longing of the heart, the desire of the mind

dohas.saralarth: On Monday keep watch day and night — drive away the longing of the heart.
dohas.gahraBhav: Monday — the day of the Moon, which governs the mind. 'Drive away the heart's longing' — bring the desires of the mind under control.

dohas.title: Mangal man ki maala phero...
dohas.fullText: Mangal man ki maala phero, chaudah koti jeet jam jero || 4 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Tuesday — the day of Mars
Tell the rosary within the mind
Subdue Yama, bring death under control

dohas.saralarth: On Tuesday tell the rosary within the mind — conquer and subdue the fourteen crore messengers of Yama.
dohas.gahraBhav: Tuesday — the day of strength and courage. 'The rosary of the mind' — inner recitation. 'Subdue Yama' — victory over the fear of death.

dohas.title: Budh vinaani vidya deejai...
dohas.fullText: Budh vinaani vidya deejai, sat sukrit nij sumiran keejai || 5 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Wednesday — the day of Mercury
Knowledge and learning
Good and true deeds
Remembrance of the Self

dohas.saralarth: On Wednesday may learning and knowledge be granted — do good deeds and remember the Self.
dohas.gahraBhav: Wednesday — the day of intellect and learning. 'Remembrance of the Self' — to remember one's own self is self-knowledge.

dohas.title: Brihaspati abhyaas bhaye bairaaga...
dohas.fullText: Brihaspati abhyaas bhaye bairaaga, taante man raate anuraaga || 6 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Thursday — the day of Jupiter
Through practice dispassion arose
The mind was dyed in loving devotion

dohas.saralarth: On Thursday, through practice dispassion arose — and then the mind was dyed in loving devotion.
dohas.gahraBhav: Thursday — the day of the Guru and Jupiter. 'Dispassion through practice' — through constant practice both dispassion and devotion are born.

dohas.title: Shukr shaala karm bataaya...
dohas.fullText: Shukr shaala karm bataaya, jad man maan sarovar nhaaya || 7 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Friday — the day of Venus
The work of the school — the schooling
Bathed in the Mansarovar lake

dohas.saralarth: On Friday the schooling was taught — when the mind bathed in the Mansarovar.
dohas.gahraBhav: Friday — the day of art and beauty. 'Bathed in the Mansarovar' — when the mind is pure, knowledge is attained.

dohas.title: Shanishchar swaasa maahin samoya...
dohas.fullText: Shanishchar swaasa maahin samoya, jab ham makartaar mag joya || 8 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Saturday — the day of Saturn
Merged within the breath
Beheld the path of the Capricorn-star

dohas.saralarth: On Saturday I merged within the breath — when I beheld the path of the Capricorn-star.
dohas.gahraBhav: Saturday — the day of patience and discipline. 'Merged within the breath' — to merge the Supreme Being into the breath is the unspoken recitation (ajapa jaap).

dohas.title: Raahu Ketu rokain nahin ghaata...
dohas.fullText: Raahu Ketu rokain nahin ghaata, Satguru kholen bajar kapaata || 9 ||

shabdarth.meaning: The two shadow-planets — held to be inauspicious
The path, the passage
The adamantine doors

dohas.saralarth: Rahu and Ketu cannot block the path — the Satguru opens the adamantine doors.
dohas.gahraBhav: Even the inauspicious planets of astrology become powerless in the shelter of the Satguru. 'Opening the adamantine doors' — the Satguru removes every obstacle.

dohas.title: Nau grah min karain nirvaana...
dohas.fullText: Nau grah min karain nirvaana, anbigat naam niraalambh jaana || 10 ||

shabdarth.meaning: The nine planets bow
Nirvana — liberation
Knew the supportless

dohas.saralarth: The nine planets bow down — having known the imperceptible, supportless Name.
dohas.gahraBhav: Even the nine planets bow before that supreme Name. 'The supportless Name' — that which is without any prop.

dohas.title: Nau grah naad samoye naasa...
dohas.fullText: Nau grah naad samoye naasa, sahans kamal dal keenha baasa || 11 ||

shabdarth.meaning: The sound merged within the nostrils
The Sahasrara lotus — the thousand-petalled

dohas.saralarth: The sound of the nine planets merged within the nostrils — and took up its dwelling in the Sahasrara.
dohas.gahraBhav: The powers of the nine planets are within the breath of the nostrils. 'Dwelt in the thousand-petalled lotus' — their abode is in the Sahasrara.

dohas.title: Dishaasool dahon dis ka khoya...
dohas.fullText: Dishaasool dahon dis ka khoya, niraalambh nirbhay pad joya || 12 ||

shabdarth.meaning: The affliction of the directions — directional ill-omen
The ten directions
The supportless and fearless state

dohas.saralarth: The directional ill-omens of all ten directions were lost — the supportless, fearless state was beheld.
dohas.gahraBhav: When union with the Supreme Being is attained, the fear of directions remains no more. 'Supportless and fearless' — that state in which there is no fear.

dohas.title: Kathin visham gati rahan hamaari...
dohas.fullText: Kathin visham gati rahan hamaari, koi na jaanat hai nar naari || 13 ||

shabdarth.meaning: A difficult and uneven path
Any man or woman

dohas.saralarth: Our way of being is difficult and uneven — no man or woman knows it.
dohas.gahraBhav: The course of the Supreme Being is mysterious. 'None knows it' — it cannot be known by the ordinary intellect.

dohas.title: Chandra samool chintaamani paaya...
dohas.fullText: Chandra samool chintaamani paaya, Garibdaas pad padhi samaaya || 14 ||

shabdarth.meaning: The moon together with its root
Found the wish-fulfilling jewel
State merged into state — absorbed in the supreme station

dohas.saralarth: Having found the wish-fulfilling jewel together with the root of the moon — Garibdas merged into the supreme station.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Chintamani' — that jewel which removes all cares. 'State merged into state' — the soul's absorption into the supreme station — this is the final conclusion of the Ramaini.

dohas.title: Aarti Anna Dev tumhaari...
dohas.fullText:
Aarti Anna Dev tumhaari, jaasain kaaya palai hamaari.
Roti aadi roo roti ant, roti hi koon gaave sant.
