Roti madhya siddh sab saadh, roti deva agam agaadh.
Roti hi ke baajain toor, roti anant lok bharpoor.
Roti hi ke Raadha rambh, roti hi ke hain rankhambh.
Raavan maangan gaya choon, taatai Lank bhai beroon.
Maandi baaji khele jooaa, roti hi par Kairon Paando mwa.
Roti pooja aatm dev, roti hi parmaatm sev.
Roti hi ke hain sab rang, roti bina na jeete jang.
Roti maangi Gorakh Naath, roti bina na chale jamaat.
Roti Krishn Dev koon paai, sahans athaasi ki khudhya mitaai.
Tandul vipra koon diye dekh, rachi Sudaamaapuri alekh.
Aadheen Vidur ghar bhojan paai, Kairon bode maan badaai.
Maan badaai sain Hari door, aajiz ke Hari sada hajoor.
Buk baakla diye vichaar, bhaye chakve kaeek baar.
Beethal hokar roti paai, Naam Dev ki kala badhaai.
Dhana bhagat koon diya beej, jaaka khet nipaaya reejh.
Drupat suta koon deenhi leer, jaakai anant badhaaye cheer.
Roti chaar bhaarija ghaali, Narseela ki hundi jhaali.
Saanwal Shaah sada ka sahi, jaaki hundi tatt lahi.
Jad koon doodh pilaaya jaan, pooja khaay gaye paashaan.
Bali koon jag rachi ashwamegh, baavan ho kar aaye umed.
Teen paid jag diya daan, baavan koon Bali chhale nidaan.
Nit bun kapda dete bhaai, jaake naulakh baalad aai.
Avgati Kesho naam Kabir, taatai chhootain jam janjeer.
Roti timar lang koon deenhi, taatai saat paadshaahi leenhi.
Roti hi ke raaj roo paat, roti hi ke hain gaj thaat.
Roti maata roti pita, roti kaatain sakal bitha.
Daas Garib kahe darvesa, roti baanto sada hamesha.
Saakhi — Garib buniya aur Baajeed ji, sunhi ke aanand.
Roti chaaron mukti hai, kate gale ke phand ||

shabdarth.meaning: The deity of grain — Annapurna
By which the body is nourished
The trumpet — the instrument of victory
Radha and Rambha — celestial beauties
Pillars of battle — warriors
Ruined, destroyed
The Kauravas and Pandavas perished
Satisfied the hunger
Rice
Sudamapuri — indescribably (alekh) beautiful
The humble, the lowly
A handful of beans (grain)
Chakva birds — separated lovers
Vitthal — Lord Krishna
A bill of promise, a draft
The dark-hued Lord (Sahib)
The imperceptible Keshav
Timur Lang — Tamerlane
Seven kingdoms
Dervish — a mendicant
Buniya and Bayazid — Sufi saints
Bread itself is the fourfold liberation
The noose about the neck — bondage

dohas.saralarth: This is the aarti of the grain-deity, by which our body is nourished. Bread is the beginning and bread is the end — even the saints sing of bread. Through bread come the adepts and the holy, and the bestowers of bread are unreachable and fathomless. Through bread the trumpet sounds — through bread the countless worlds are filled. Radha and Rambha are of bread; the warrior-pillars are of bread. Ravana went to beg for flour — and so Lanka was ruined. The Kauravas and Pandavas fought over bread and perished. Bread is the worship of the soul-deity; bread is the service of the Supreme. All splendours are of bread — without bread no battle is won. Gorakhnath begged for bread; without bread no assembly proceeds. Krishna received bread and satisfied the hunger of eighty-eight thousand. Seeing Sudama's rice, he raised the indescribable Sudamapuri. He took food in the humble Vidura's home, while he kept the proud Kauravas at a distance — for Hari stays far from pride and ever near the humble. He gave thought to a handful of beans and was reborn many times as a chakva. As Vitthal he received bread and exalted Namdev's glory. He gave seed to Dhana the devotee and joyfully tilled his field. To Draupadi he gave cloth, lengthening it without end. He made bread for four wives and honoured Narsi's draft — the dark-hued Lord, ever true, who fulfilled the draft on the instant. He drank milk offered to stone, and went away as the stone was worshipped. For Bali he arranged the horse-sacrifice and came as the dwarf (Vamana); begging three steps of land, the dwarf at last subdued Bali. He daily wove cloth, and brought ninety lakh bullock-loads. The imperceptible Keshav by the name of Kabir — by it the chains of Yama fall away. He gave bread to Timur Lang, and through it gained seven kingdoms. Sovereignty and throne are of bread; royal grandeur is of bread. Bread is mother, bread is father — bread cuts away every grief. The servant Garib, the dervish, says: share your bread always. Sakhi — Buniya and Bayazid found bliss in hearing this: bread itself is the fourfold liberation, and it cuts the noose about the neck.
dohas.gahraBhav: The Aarti of the grain-deity — this is not merely praise of food, but a revelation of the very essence of life. 'Bread is the beginning and bread is the end' — both the origin and the end of creation are bound up with food. 'Bread is the fourfold liberation' — to share bread is itself righteousness, wealth, fulfilment and liberation. The many tales of devotees show that the Supreme Being has always played his divine sport on the pretext of bread. 'Hari is ever near the humble' — to one who is humble and lowly, Hari is always near. This aarti gives the highest message of equality and sharing.
